Hi Tom / Priya —

Great to chat earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a focused benchmark:

Summary from call:
- Target p95 latency: <= 350ms for interactive assistant flows (this was called out as a hard SLO).
- Typical request shape: 1) long user context + system prompt (variable) -> 2) model-generated assistant response.
- Current ask: up to ~12k tokens of input in peak cases; typical session ~4k. Output target for assistant responses ~512–2k tokens depending on task.
- Concurrency/throughput: expected sustained throughput ~120 req/s during business hours, bursts to ~200 req/s.
- Streaming: required for the chat assistant to reduce time-to-first-byte; batch embedding/analytic jobs are non-streaming.

Action items / clarifying questions for you (so we can run the right perf tests):
1) Can you confirm the absolute max input tokens you want us to test (we heard 12k but want to be explicit)?
2) For streaming: do you need partial tokens for every request (i.e., always stream), or only for sessions flagged interactive?
3) Any hard constraints on model variants (e.g., must be quantized / 8-bit) or can we run non-quantized for baseline?

I attached a short performance_requirements.xlsx — if you can drop a sample prompt + 10 representative conversations there, we’ll use those for the benchmark.

Next steps from our side once you confirm: SE-run benchmark against a Dedicated pool (or Hosted if you prefer) and share p50/p95/p99 numbers for the prompt set and the exact context sizes.

Tom / Priya —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. Below are pragmatic p95 estimates and configuration notes based on similar customers and our Dedicated pool configurations. These are estimates — we'll bench with your exact prompts and traffic pattern to produce final numbers.

High-level p95 guidance (per request; single-turn generation where noted):
- 12k input + 1k output / fp16 model on A100-class hardware: p95 ~ 400–700 ms (depends on model family and tokenization overhead).
- 12k input + 1k output / quantized 8-bit variant on A100-class or equivalent: p95 ~ 550–900 ms (quantization trades CPU/GPU kernels and can increase memory/permute overhead; we often see ~1.2x–1.4x tail latency vs fp16 for very long contexts).
- 4k input + 512 output / quantized: p95 ~ 200–350 ms (this is in-line with your 350ms SLO for typical cases).

Notes about what drives latency at long context windows:
- Tokenization & encoding: longer inputs increase encoder time linearly before generation begins.
- KV cache lookups + attention: for causal generation the KV cache size grows with context and can add memory pressure and jitter at tail.
- Memory swaps / kernel selection: very long context windows sometimes hit different kernels (or require tiled attention) which increases per-token overhead.
- Batching: small micro-batches help amortize kernel launch overhead; but at high concurrency, increased batching can add queuing latency.

Streaming vs non-streaming:
- Streaming (server-sent tokens) improves perceived latency — time-to-first-byte typically drops significantly (often <100–200 ms for short outputs) because we start flushing partial tokens as they’re produced.
- Total end-to-end time to produce full 1k tokens remains governed by token generation speed; streaming primarily improves UX for interactive sessions.

Concurrency guidance and tuning:
- Per-replica concurrency recommendation: start with 6–8 concurrent inferences per replica for 13B-class models on GPU to balance GPU utilization vs tail latency. Increase to 12–16 for 7B-class models.
- If you need high sustained qPS (120 rps) with p95 targets, we recommend Dedicated capacity with autoscaling + burst pool. That gives predictable latency and isolation for noisy neighbors.
- Multi-replica horizontal scaling is preferable to cramming high concurrency on fewer replicas — tail latency rises non-linearly beyond recommended concurrency.

Recommendations for FinCo’s requirements:
1) Use streaming for the chat assistant to meet perceived latency SLOs.
2) Default to an 8-bit quantized variant for cost — but run a quick fp16 baseline during bench to measure delta. If p95 for 12k+1k in quantized > SLA, consider fp16 or a larger Dedicated pool.
3) KV/prefix caching: enable caching for frequently re-used system prompts to reduce effective context costs where applicable.
4) Autoscaling & burst capacity: configure Dedicated pool with steady baseline to cover 120 rps and burst nodes for 200 rps to protect p95.

Deliverables we’ll produce once you approve the test set:
- Per-prompt p50/p95/p99 for your sample prompts at 3 context sizes (4k, 8k, 12k).
- Time-to-first-byte (TTFB) numbers for streaming and non-streaming.
- Recommendation: concurrency per-replica and Dedicated pool sizing.

I attached expected_latency_by_context_window.csv (estimates) and redwood_perf_summary.pdf (customer-facing summary).

Proposed next step: we’ll run the benchmark next week if that timeline works — SE load test + 5 business days for analysis and report. Does Mon 6/29 or Tue 6/30 work to kick this off?

Thanks,
Marissa
